art.subject: Willow Warbler (Phylloscopus trochilus), adult on autumn passage, of the greyish eastern form that reaches East Asia: upperparts plain greyish olive-brown with a faint greenish tinge on the rump and on the edges of the wing and tail feathers; a long pale yellowish-white supercilium from the bill base to well behind the eye and a dusky eye-stripe; ear-coverts mottled; underparts whitish with a faint pale yellow wash on the throat and breast and greyish-buff breast sides; no wing-bars; fine bill, dark with a pale pinkish-yellow base to the lower mandible; dark eye; pale pinkish-brown legs.
art.pose: foraging among willow leaves, side view, reaching for an insect
art.scene: willow and shrub thicket on a Korean offshore island during autumn migration in September, soft morning light; no people, buildings or text
views: adult on autumn passage, eastern greyish form, side view perched among willow leaves: slim, elongated leaf warbler with a flattish crown, long pale supercilium, dusky eye-stripe, greyish olive upperparts, no wing-bars, long primary projection reaching well down the tail, whitish underparts washed pale yellow, pale pinkish-brown legs

adult, three-quarter front view on a willow twig: long pale supercilium over a dusky eye-stripe, greyish olive head and back, whitish underparts with a faint yellow wash on the throat and breast, long wings, pale pinkish-brown legs
art.build: A small, slim leaf warbler, smaller than a sparrow and slightly larger and longer-winged than a Yellow-browed Warbler; sleek and elongated with a flattish crown and no crest. Bill thin and pointed, shorter than the head. Legs medium and slender, pale pinkish-brown. Long wings: at rest the primary projection beyond the tertials is long, and the wingtips reach well down the tail. Tail medium, plain, square-ended to slightly notched. Gleans actively in foliage and occasionally dips the tail.
avoid: Do not add wing-bars; that would make it an Arctic or Two-barred Warbler.
Do not paint blackish legs (Common Chiffchaff, Dusky Warbler); this species has pale pinkish-brown legs.
Do not paint bright lemon-yellow throat and breast with a pure white belly (Wood Warbler); this form is mostly whitish below.
Do not add a crown stripe or a pale rump patch (Pallas's Leaf Warbler).
